title: Physical sky with a matching sun lamp
purpose: Build a physical sky world and a sun lamp whose direction matches the sky's sun exactly, from one elevation and compass bearing, with the sky's sun disc off so the lamp gives sharp direct light. Use it for exteriors, architecture and time-of-day studies.

parameters.name: azimuth
parameters.description: Compass bearing of the sun, clockwise from +Y (0 is +Y, 90 is +X).

parameters.name: sun_angle
parameters.description: Angular diameter of the sun lamp; larger values soften shadows.

parameters.name: sky_sun_disc
parameters.description: Also draw the sun disc in the sky texture (it then lights the scene as well).

parameters.name: air_density
parameters.description: Air density of the sky model.

parameters.name: haze
parameters.description: Dust or aerosol density of the sky model.

outputs.description: A world named Baltor Sky set as the scene world, and a sun lamp named Baltor Sky Sun.

limits: The bearing convention (clockwise from +Y, as the Sky Texture sun rotation) was measured on Blender 5.2.1 only. Uses the multiple scattering sky where Blender offers it and the Nishita sky otherwise; their colours differ. Lamp strength is a free parameter, not derived from the sky model, so sky and sun brightness are balanced by eye. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
technique_references: Sun direction from elevation and bearing on the unit sphere
Light rotation that points a lamp's -Z axis along a direction
Equirectangular panorama render used to measure the sky's sun convention
